newsitem.title: DUBAI: Saudi stocks rise in busy trade.
newsitem.headline: Saudi stocks rise in busy trade.

text.p: Saudi Arabia's stock market ended the week to Thursday higher in busy trade focusing on bank and cement companies shares, the Riyadh-based Bakheet Financial Advisors (BFA) said.
The all-share index closed 2.73 percent higher at 174.32 from 169.68 points the previous week.
Of the 59 shares traded during the week, 40 rose, eight fell and 11 were unchanged.
The BFA put trading value at about 2.17 billion riyals ($578 million) up from last week's 1.18 billion. About nine million shares exchanged hands in the week up from last week's 5.6 million shares.
Tabuk Cement was the week's major gainer closing 10.6 percent higher at 146 riyals from 132 riyals the previous week.
Among other gainers in the week was Arab National Bank which ended the week at 501 riyals from 458 riyals a week earlier.
United Saudi Commercial gained about nine percent on a bonus share issue to shareholders of one free share for evry four shares held. The share price closed at 293 riyals from 268 riyals last week.
Main decliner in the week was Zoujaj whose stock slumped to 166 riyals from 175 the previous week.
Also declining was al-Mawashi al-Mukalrish whose share fell to 92 riyals from 93 the earlier week.
